Definition: of foreign origin (compare H3646); dill or fennel ("cummin"):--cummin.
BiblicalUsage: Cummin is the small seed the Pharisees tithed, and it appears once, in Jesus' woe in Matthew 23:23: they pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, "and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith."
TheologicalSignificance: In my reading, this cummin seed is the whole rebuke in miniature: they measured the smallest herb to the last grain and missed the justice and mercy the law was about.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
